claims.text: The base Cr16Mn16Fe16Co16Ni16P20 alloy forms several primary non-eutectic crystalline phases.
The base alloy exhibits a complex, multistep crystallization sequence during cooling and reheating.
The base alloy exhibits extensive primary crystallization and limited amorphous-phase retention even under rapid cooling.
The proposed intervention is to introduce approximately 3 at.% boron into the base alloy.
Approximately 3 at.% boron will suppress primary non-eutectic crystallization during cooling.
Approximately 3 at.% boron will raise the onset temperature of crystallization during reheating.
Boron addition will increase amorphous retention and thermal stability relative to the unmodified alloy.
Boron addition will increase atomic-level disorder and lattice strain.
The increased disorder and lattice strain will inhibit nucleation and growth of primary crystalline phases.
Boron has a small atomic size relative to the principal alloying elements.
Boron will enhance atomic-size mismatch and modify short-range order in this alloy.
Enhanced atomic-size mismatch and modified short-range order will increase the nucleation-energy barrier and make crystalline nuclei less favorable.
Increasing the nucleation barrier will retard primary crystallization during cooling and delay crystallization during reheating.
The boron-modified alloy will have a broader processing window for amorphous-phase formation than the base alloy.
The boron-modified alloy will exhibit less primary crystallization during slower cooling than the base alloy.
The intervention is expected to be effective at cooling rates above approximately 10^5 K/s.
The benefit of boron addition may diminish at very low cooling rates or extreme reheating rates.
